messages:
maya: Quick heads-up: the 'llamacore' Next.js starter (Next Edge + LangChain wiring) is surfacing intermittent 401s in staging. Locally can't repro.

ben: Do you have the minimal handler? Edge vs Node differences matter.

maya: Handler is tiny: ```js
import { createClient } from 'redwood-sdk'
const client = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY })
export default async function handler(req) {
  const { prompt } = await req.json()
  const r = await client.generate({ model: 'gpt-compat', prompt })
  return new Response(JSON.stringify(r))
}
```
No explicit refresh logic. SDK should handle refresh but we see ~1% 401s in staging when traffic spikes.

carol: That sounds like the refresh lock race in edge-like runtimes. We implemented a mutex in node but not in web/edge. When token expires multiple inflight requests race to refresh and some still go out with old token.

ben: Short-term for the starter: add an opt-in wrapper that retries once on 401 with small jitter. Show it in README under "Edge auth tip" so users don't ship it blindly.

maya: I added RW_EDGE_RETRY=true to the starter env and a tiny retry helper in the api template. PR created: maya/llamacore-edge-retry.

carol: I'll own the SDK fix. Plan: implement a lightweight web-safe mutex (Promise-based) that works in both Node and Edge, ensure single refresh attempt, and have inflight callers wait and then retry automatically. Add tests in our edge emulator with 100 concurrent requests.

ben: Also add CI spike test in sample repo: run 500 concurrent requests to /api/generate and fail build if >0.5% 401/5xx. That prevents regressions in the starter.

ci-bot: CI: integration job queued for maya/llamacore-edge-retry (node + edge-emulator).

maya: Thanks. I'll link the SDK issue in the PR. Once SDK patch lands we should remove the sample wrapper and update the README to recommend the native SDK behavior.

carol: ETA for SDK patch: EOW. I'll add unit + integration tests and a changelog note.

ben: Also add a short paragraph to the starter README about token choice: recommend long-lived keys for quick starters or use server-side refresh proxy if you need hosted short-lived keys in edge. Explain tradeoffs.

maya: Sounds good. PR description includes that text. Reviewers: @ben @carol.

ci-bot: CI: integration failed (401 rate 1.2%). Attaching logs to #sdk/edge-refresh for investigation.

maya: Will monitor. Thanks for the fast triage. :sparkles:
